channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: With new law, Iraq sees rise in child marriage, custody battles
item.description: In January 2025, Iraq's parliament passed an amendment allowing families to place their household under religious law, governing all issues around marriage, divorce and inheritance. The new Ja'fari law, a Shiite law, came into force in October 2025. One year on, its consequences have been raising serious alarm, especially among women, who say they've seen a major rollback of their rights. FRANCE 24's Marie-Charlotte Roupie reports, with Josh Vardey.

item.title: Japan's radical past: Retracing the far-left groups of the 1970s
item.description: Our correspondents delve into the history of Japan's radical left in the 1970s. From the United Red Army to the Japanese Red Army, several movements turned to armed struggle and violent action. More than half a century on, our team met with two former militants.

item.title: WATCH: The Children's Hospital Thanksgiving Day Parade
item.description: Staff and families put on their own Thanksgiving Day parade at Cook Children's Medical Center in Fort Worth, Texas.

item.title: Kenyan cult leader in jail for 191 murders convicted over another 123 deaths
item.description: A Kenyan cult leader has been convicted of manslaughter over the deaths of 123 of his followers, having already been found guilty of murdering 191 others.

item.title: Republicans rethink tariffs, giving Democrats an opening to challenge Trump
item.description: Democrats are looking to blunt some of President Donald Trump's tariffs as they take control of Congress

item.title: Poundland boss urges staff to feel pride in turnaround efforts
item.description: Poundland's boss has told staff to feel proud of their efforts to revitalise the discount retailer despite its collapse into administration earlier this week.

item.title: Thanksgiving storm damages buildings, floods streets, causes power outages
item.description: Strong winds ripped the roof off a building in Maryland, as an extreme storm began to move up the East Coast on Thanksgiving morning.

item.title: US: Thanksgiving storms cause flooding and travel chaos
item.description: Severe storms battered the US East Coast on Thursday, bringing torrential rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. Nearly one million homes were left without power, while hundreds of flights were cancelled and thousands delayed during one of the country's busiest travel periods. The weather also forced the postponement of New York's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday.

item.title: Black Friday: The evolution of a shopping phenomenon
item.description: Once defined by crowds queuing outside shops for one-off bargains, Black Friday has evolved into weeks of online promotions. As discounts spread throughout the year, consumers are becoming more cautious about advertised deals, increasingly turning to AI and price comparisons to find genuine bargains. Camille Knight looks at the origins of the global shopping phenomenon.

item.title: Zelenskyy urges the US to pressure Putin, calling Trump’s 'my friend' remark strange
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is expressing frustration with the U.S. approach to Russian leader Vladimir Putin

item.title: Ukraine: Residents brace for another difficult winter
item.description: As Russia continues to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure, residents are preparing for another difficult winter of strikes and power cuts. With supply chains under pressure, food prices are also rising, forcing many Ukrainians to cut back on essentials or stock up ahead of the coming months.

item.title: Spain election: Housing crisis and immigration dominate final campaign debate
item.description: Spain goes to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election that may usher in a right-wing coalition to replace the Socialist-led minority government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, one of Europe's last leftist leaders. Our correspondent Sarah Morris tells us more.

item.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
item.description: The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.

item.title: Kuwait: Two Italians killed in drone attack
item.description: A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working on an air defence system on Thursday, marking the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months.

item.title: EU: Leaders fail to reach agreement on next budget after tense summit
item.description: At the bloc headquarters in Brussels on Thursday, EU leaders failed to reach a consensus after more than 12 hours of talks over the budget and a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s economic and military needs next year. France 24's Dave Keating tells us more.

item.title: WATCH: 12-year-old soccer star turns hearing loss into inspiration
item.description: ABC News' Danny New has the story of Delaney Anbardan, a young soccer player in Southern California who has continued pursuing the sport while navigating progressive hearing loss.

item.title: Israel's Eisenkot reaches deal with left-wing faction as coalition talks gain steam
item.description: Gadi ​Eisenkot's Yashar party and a left-wing faction agreed on a preliminary coalition deal on Thursday, after a brief dispute that had posed a challenge to his bid to unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following an inconclusive election last month. France 24's Andrew Hilliar tells us more.

item.title: UN warns hunger will deepen in the Middle East
item.description: Hunger is expected to worsen in 16 countries over the next six months, with Sudan and Yemen among five nations at the highest level of concern, the U.N.’s food agencies warned Friday

item.title: US Air Force's cloud computing platform hacked
item.description: The US Air Force's (USAF) flagship cloud computing platform has been hacked, people with knowledge of the incident have said.

item.title: Immigration: South Africa no longer an El Dorado for foreigners
item.description: South Africa was once a welcoming country; a refuge for those fleeing conflict and persecution. But for thousands of foreigners, the dream of a new life in South Africa is turning into more of a nightmare. Against a backdrop of unemployment and economic hardship, anti-immigration movements are gaining ground. Our correspondents report.

item.title: From Thanksgiving blackouts to Black Friday, a holiday hit by wild weather and economic woes
item.description: A storm battered much of the country on Thursday, knocking out power to thousands of homes and disrupting travel. Today, Black Friday shopping deals kick off, and on Saturday New York City will hold the postponed Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

item.title: Spain’s Pedro makes final campaign push to beat the right ahead of crunch vote
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez makes his final campaign push with a rally in Madrid Friday, the last day of campaigning for Sunday's high-stakes elections. Opinion polls show the Socialist premier lagging behind the main right-wing Popular Party (PP) as the Spanish vote opens an electoral cycle over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the EU.

item.title: Powerful storm knocks out power and disrupts flights in US - as major Thanksgiving event cancelled
item.description: Powerful storms across the US have left hundreds of thousands of homes without power and disrupted thousands of flights ahead of Thanksgiving weekend.

item.title: Israel's Eisenkot and left-wing party agree coalition deal
item.description: The centrist party of Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form the next Israeli government, and an allied left-wing party on Thursday announced they had agreed on a coalition deal.

item.title: Spain general election 2026: Could Sánchez lose power?
item.description: Spanish voters head to the polls in just three days for a snap election, after eight years of Socialist-led rule. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is fighting to stay in power, but an alliance between the conservative People's Party and the far-right VOX could bring his time in office to an end. So what are the key issues, and what's at stake?

item.title: EU leaders split over budget spending and a $49 billion loan to Ukraine
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron set an end-of-year deadline for an agreement on the European Union's next seven-year budget after the continent's leaders ruled out any chances for a deal to be reached at their summit on Thursday.

item.title: Live: Trump calls on Putin to end all 'military aggression' against Europe
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had urged his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe". Although Trump did not provide any further details, he added that he hoped this would pave the way for a peace deal to be struck between Kyiv and Moscow. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: Can luxury save Macy's?
item.description: This week's celebration of Macy's 100th Thanksgiving parade finds the department store at a turning point. After years of losing sales, the retailer is reimagining itself — as a higher-end destination.

item.title: Screen free tweens try their hand at Dungeons & Dragons
item.description: Some parents, fed up with screens, have found an analog oasis in the role-playing game invented in the 1970s.

item.title: Trump effectively ended asylum. Advocates look to the Supreme Court to restore it
item.description: Trump's sweeping immigration changes — an asylum ban, mass firings and new legal maneuvers — have all but ended asylum. The high court will soon consider whether some shifts deny people due process.

item.title: 12 strategies to cut your risk of dementia. Take this quiz to start
item.description: Here's something you can do as you gather with family and friends this holiday season: Take a free, five-minute quiz to assess your brain health. You'll learn simple changes to keep your mind sharp.

item.title: Why is India so afraid of Pakistan's new Netflix series?
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 27: Controversy brews as India asks Netflix to ban a Pakistani series from being broadcast in the country. Tensions have been high between the two nations since last year's terror attack in the Kashmir region. Also in the news: Taiwanese voters will head to the polls for all-important local elections overshadowed by the threat of Chinese claims to the island. Finally, forget schadenfreude – practicing "freudenfreude" is better for your health.

item.title: Five people hospitalised as Levski Sofia and Marseille fans clash ahead of Europa League game
item.description: Fighting broke out ahead of Thursday's Europa League match between Levski Sofia and Olympique Marseille, with five Bulgarian fans ending up in hospital. Local media reported a number of Levski fans performing Nazi salutes in the lead-up to the skirmish.

item.title: Centrica warns on jobs after government snubs Rough gas storage deal
item.description: The FTSE-100 utility Centrica has warned that hundreds of jobs at its Rough gas storage facility off the Yorkshire coast are at risk and claimed that ministers had rejected proposals to bolster Britain's energy security.

item.title: Eagles rally to stun Cowboys coming back from 21 points behind
item.description: Eagles QB Joe Milton threw two long touchdowns against the quarterback's former team, the Dallas Cowboys, for the the start of quite a comeback, after being down 31-10 early in the third quarter.

item.title: France and Germany push for EU budget deal by year-end as far-right rise threatens Ukraine aid
item.description: As Europe braces itself for a slew of tense elections in 2027, Paris and Berlin are pushing for the European Union to strike a budget deal by December 31 to lock in financial aid for Ukraine. But Thursday's talks in Brussels seem to have done little to build consensus around the bloc's next budget.

item.title: 'Tribal loyalty' works on right: 'Heart on the left' sensitive to racism, anti-Semitism
item.description: As French far-right leader Jordan Bardella denies fresh allegations concerning anti-Semitic remarks he allegedly made as a teenager, how much damage could the affair do to Marine Le Pen's presidential prospects? Ana Navarro Pedro, correspondent for Portuguese media, believes its electoral impact may be limited, despite Le Pen's defence of Bardella and her choice of him as a future prime minister. "What they most regret in this whole episode is that Bardella is denying it," she says of prospective Le Pen voters.

item.title: MoD can't find contact details for half of veterans
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has published open letters to almost 100,000 veterans about their duty to mobilise in a crisis but it appears unable to find many people's direct contact details.

item.title: Almost a million Americans left without power on Thanksgiving as storm sweeps East Coast
item.description: Nearly a million people were left without power Thursday after a severe storm lashed the East Coast of the US, tearing up trees and powerlines on Thanksgiving. New York City authorities had been forced to postpone the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade due to the intense winds.

item.title: Israel's Eisenkot agrees to coalition deal with left-wing Democrats
item.description: Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot on Thursday struck a coalition deal with Yair Golan's left-leaning Democrats, bringing the country's opposition closer to forming a government after no single bloc secured a majority in the October elections.

item.title: Lyon held and Marseille pushed in mixed Europa League night for French clubs
item.description: There were mixed fortunes for the French clubs in Thursday's Europa League action, as Marseille saw off Levski Sofia (1-0) in the only win of the night. Lyon were held at home by Lillestrom of Norway, while Rennes fell to Dutch side Nijmegen.

item.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state, has died
item.description: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.

item.title: Amazon staff to strike and rally on busiest weekend of the year
item.description: Amazon employees around the world are set to stage protests on Black Friday amid claims of unfair pay and oppressive working conditions.

item.title: WATCH: Tips for navigating the holiday travel rush
item.description: The Points Guy Clint Henderson provides some tips and tricks travelers can use to navigate the Thanksgiving weekend.

item.title: Black Friday hype stems from a desire 'to be part of a collective event', expert says
item.description: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".

item.title: WATCH: The tradition of Thanksgiving
item.description: ABC News' Michelle Franzen takes us to Plymouth, Massachusetts, where the tradition of Thanksgiving began when English settlers shared a meal with native tribes.

item.title: RN’s antisemitic past ‘coming back to haunt them’: Will Le Pen ‘distance herself’ from Bardella?
item.description: Could new allegations of antisemitism damage Jordan Bardella’s standing and the far-right National Rally’s electoral prospects? Charli James is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. Smith examines the far-right leader’s continued denials and considers whether Marine Le Pen might eventually distance herself from him. In the meantime, Smith suggests that Bardella needs to “make his mind up” about how to respond to these latest troubling allegations published by Le Monde and Mediapart. “It’s very difficult to deny. Le Monde and Mediapart, certainly Le Monde, wouldn’t be publishing these details if they didn’t have some pretty substantial evidence.” Could this prove to be the Achilles’ heel of a far-right party with its sights set on the second round of the presidential election?

item.title: WATCH: Viral Thanksgiving story set to be adapted for small screen
item.description: Jamal Hinton and Wanda Dench's viral story of a wrong text that led to a decadelong Thanksgiving tradition is set to become a Lifetime production. Will Ganss shares the buzziest stories in Pop News.

item.title: Driver suspected of causing tanker crash in Egypt that killed 31 detained
item.description: The driver of a car suspected to have caused a fuel tanker to overturn in Egypt, causing the deaths of 31 people, has been detained.

item.title: Witnesses contacted as US probe into World Cup sell-off plan intensifies
item.description: A planned US congressional investigation into FIFA and Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plans is intensifying with requests to speak to current and former FIFA staff, Sky News understands.

item.title: Iran live updates: Iranian drone attack killed 2 Italians, Kuwait says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Airline suspends all flights - as carrier faces bankruptcy
item.description: Norse Atlantic Airways has suspended all flights, with the company saying it could file for bankruptcy unless an urgent solution to its finances is found.

item.title: WATCH: NYPD releases new images in manhole mystery
item.description: In the latest on the ongoing manhole mystery in New York City, the NYPD has released new images of suspects seen exiting a manhole last week.

item.title: WATCH: Women around the world fight for gender equity in sumo
item.description: For more than 1,500 years, professional sumo has only allowed men into the ring. Nightline traveled to Japan to learn more about the ancient ban and meet with athletes fighting against tradition.

item.title: WATCH: Man uses balloon art to pay off $400K in student loans
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a doctor in New York who's using his balloon twisting talents to help him pay off his student loan debt.

item.title: Myanmar says it will not comply with 'inappropriate' ICJ genocide orders
item.description: Myanmar's leader has said his government will not ‌comply with all measures ordered by a top international court after it was found guilty of committing genocide against the Rohingya minority.

item.title: Major US tech index comes close to crashing into a bear market
item.description: A tech-heavy index on Wall Street briefly teetered into bear market territory on Wednesday - as AI-exposed stocks continue to face heavy sell-offs.

item.title: WATCH: Tips for staying healthy and keeping the peace at the Thanksgiving table
item.description: Nutrition specialist J.J. Virgin and etiquette expert Thomas Farley discuss how you can navigate some of Thanksgiving's tricky problems.

item.title: Trump admin proposes new tariffs on China, EU and 12 other trading partners
item.description: A senior admin official said the countries were informed of proposed tariffs.

item.title: US authorises SpaceX to deploy one million satellites to space
item.description: The US' Federal Communications Commission is authorising SpaceX to send a million satellites for data centres in space, the agency said.

item.description: Daniel Riff, head of global food access programs for DoorDash, discusses the company's initiative.

item.title: WATCH: Best and worst times to drive
item.description: ABC News' Rhiannon Ally provides the latest updates on the road as gas prices drop, offering some relief for drivers this Thanksgiving.

item.description: A D.C. magistrate judge has issued a scathing written order ripping the Trump administration for what he described as the blatant "weaponization" of law enforcement.

item.description: The White House says Melania Trump has helped return a seventh group of Ukrainian and Russian children to their families

item.title: Treasury's financial crimes agency says it's investigating 'cybersecurity incident'
item.description: The agency handles sensitive information and reports about financial crimes.

item.title: WATCH: Australian man bikes 10,000 miles across 48 US states
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to ultra cyclist Jack Thompson, who rode through all 48 states in the contiguous U.S., covering almost 10,000 miles in 60 days.

item.title: Two children among six dead in plane crash
item.description: Divers have found the bodies of six people, including two children, after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi on Tuesday, according to the US Coast Guard.

item.description: Trump pardoned Giuliani last year.

item.title: They want to watch Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan die but the Army won’t let them
item.description: Julia Wilson was nine months pregnant when she found herself caught in gunfire at Fort Hood in 2009. 'It's crazy how quickly things run through your brain," she said.

item.title: Groups push back on Trump administration changes to historical monument
item.description: Two Philadelphia groups filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration over the removal of panels at the slavery memorial at the President’s House site.
